subject: dominance effect in a RIL population

messages.author: 7b7af7697383276a
messages.subject: dominance effect in a RIL population
parts:
Hi,
can you please help me to understanding the following problem?
I am using an F8 RIL population to map QTLs for 13 traits. However
some of the individuals are still heterozygous.
I will use here one of the traits as an example.
Once I have loaded the data into Rqtl I classified them as rilself.
Then I ran a scanone and subsequently a CIM analysis and obtained 2
QTL.
In order to see the variance explained by the QTL I fitted a model
y~Q1+Q2. This is the output I have obtained:

fitqtl summary

Method: Haley-Knott regression
Number of observations : 178

Full model result
----------------------------------
Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2

df SS MS LOD %var Pvalue(Chi2) Pvalue
(F)
Model 4 1462.044 365.51110 9.939028 22.67400 2.748563e-09
4.51128e-09
Error 173 4986.064
28.82118
Total 177
6448.109


Drop one QTL at a time ANOVA table:
----------------------------------
df Type III SS LOD %var F value Pvalue(Chi2) Pvalue
(F)
4...@64.0 2 647.502 4.719 10.042 11.233 1.91e-05 2.59e-05
***
6...@64.5 2 719.812 5.212 11.163 12.488 6.13e-06 8.59e-06
***
---
Signif. codes: 0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1


Estimated effects:
-----------------
est SE t
Intercept 24.1241 1.6321 14.781
4...@64.0a -1.9588 0.4585 -4.272
4...@64.0d -4.3897 2.3248 -1.888
6...@64.5a -2.2389 0.4517 -4.956
6...@64.5d -2.4993 2.4514 -1.020

In my understandind "a" represent the additive effect and "d" the
dominance effect.
As you can see in this case the "d" effect is similar or higher than
the "a" effect. This sounds odd to me as I am working with a RIL
population. One of the possible reason I can see that some of my
individuals are still het at some markers.
Here then my questions:
1) is my interpretation correct?
2) does this effect the "a" value I obtain?
3) if yes, how can I get rid of it?

One thing I have tried it is to create a nev csv file, replaced the
"H" with missing information and used the following functions:

F8oxoli <- est.rf(F8oxoli) #estimates pairwise Rf between markers
newmap <- est.map(F8oxoli, error.prob=0.01)
F8oxoli<-replace.map(F8oxoli,newmap)

and repeated the QTL analysis.
The results of this have caused results that the human being can't
describe .... :D...I concluded it is not the right way.

Thank you
Maria

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: dominance effect in a RIL population
parts:
Something is going wrong.

R/qtl can't deal with residual heterozygosity in an RIL population.

Also, with the cross type "riself", though should be just two possible
genotypes,
the drop-one-QTL table from fitqtl should give 1 df per QTL, and the
estimated
effects should just have the estimated additive effects.

karl
